headline: Law updates the 2010 Crow Tribe water rights settlement, changing how irrigation and drinking water project money is handled and extending a hydropower deadline.
what_it_does: This law changes the 2010 water rights settlement between the Crow Tribe and the state of Montana. It creates an interest-bearing account so the Bureau of Reclamation can keep fixing up the Crow Irrigation Project. It replaces the single planned community water system with broader "MR&I Projects" and sets up a new account the tribe must use for building water production, treatment, or delivery systems. It also gives the tribe five more years, until 2030, as the only party allowed to build hydropower facilities at the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Crow Tribe of Montana
who_it_affects.how: Their tribe gets new accounts and more flexibility for water infrastructure projects, plus more time to develop hydropower at the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam.

who_it_affects.group: People who live on or farm the Crow Reservation
who_it_affects.how: Work on the reservation's irrigation system and community water supply projects will be funded and managed under the revised rules.
The agency gets a new account it can use to continue repairing and improving the Crow Irrigation Project.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 15, 2026; the tribe's exclusive hydropower right is extended to 2030.
